 Dated this, the 9th day of July, 2014.
 J U D G M E N T

This writ petition is filed seeking for a direction to release Black Matpe imported as per Ext. P1 to the petitioner after giving an opportunity for completing the cleaning as permitted under Exts. P2,
P6, P9 and P10 and later conducting a fresh sampling and analysis/testing without any delay.

2. While importing the aforesaid commodity, the 1st respondent found that the same was not in accordance with the standard specified under the Food Safety and Standards Act and the Rules framed thereunder.
Thereafter, on the request of the petitioner, they were permitted to clean the commodity.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that cleaning process is almost over and if filtering is to be done and thereafter sample is taken by the 1st respondent, the same may conform to the standards prescribed.

4. Having regard to the aforesaid factual situation and having heard the learned standing counsel appearing for respondents, I am of the view that this writ petition can be disposed of as under:
The petitioner is permitted to complete the entire process of cleaning and filtering within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

It is made clear that after the entire process is completed, the 1st respondent shall take necessary sample and if it is found to be within the standards prescribed, the respondents are entitled to release the cargo to the petitioner on compliance with other formalities.
Sd/- A.M. Shaffique, Judge.
